problem: Turn P2 Honey into a meaningful permanent-power loop where the player chooses Flight or Buzz at a dedicated Hive, immediately feels the purchased effect, understands the first Buzz capability gate, cannot create a negative-Honey/customization dead-end, and keeps progression across save migration and reload on desktop and touch.

decision.rationale: Retain the validated Flight + Buzz two-track set and productionize one level of each through a dedicated two-card Hive surface. Exact-head browser evidence proves that Flight changes real traversal from 300 to 330 u/s, Buzz changes real pollination work from 1.00x to 1.35x and unlocks the explicit Lavender Buzz-2 gate, purchases are input-isolated and durable, while deterministic economy regression keeps both first-purchase orders and the customization-heavy path non-negative and progression-safe.

selected_references.name: Slime Rancher dedicated home upgrade surface
selected_references.selection_reason: Direct structural reference for a low-frequency permanent-upgrade interaction attached to a recognizable home base.
selected_references.observed_behavior: Vacpack upgrades are purchased at the ranch through a dedicated upgrade interface and entries communicate permanent capability plus price.
selected_references.inference: BeBee should place permanent Flight/Buzz purchases at the Hive rather than overloading flower interaction, and should make the purchase low-frequency and immediate.

selected_references.name: Dave the Diver current/next/price hierarchy
selected_references.selection_reason: Useful compact information-hierarchy reference for showing what changes before a permanent purchase.
selected_references.observed_behavior: The iDiver upgrade surface presents equipment level/stat progression together with price information.
selected_references.inference: Each BeBee card should expose current level/effect, next effect and Honey cost; with only Flight and Buzz validated, two complete cards are preferable to a filler third card.

selected_references.name: A Short Hike perceptible traversal upgrade
selected_references.selection_reason: Direct reference for permanent progression that changes movement capability rather than a hidden meta number.
selected_references.observed_behavior: Golden Feathers increase traversal capability in the world.
selected_references.inference: Flight must change the production movement runtime itself and be verified by measured speed after purchase.

anti_pattern.observation: Stardew Valley tool upgrades intentionally include a multi-day delivery delay and additional resource requirements.
anti_pattern.lesson: Do not add waiting/calendar friction to BeBee P3: the current problem is an immediate reward-to-power loop and no waiting problem has been validated.

official_docs.verified_constraint: Input focus is explicit and an action returned as consumed does not continue to lower recipients; the Hive reuses the modal input stack and movement must remain zero while the panel owns focus.
GUI scripts own presentation and input routing, while P3 keeps progression/economy state in domain systems rather than mutating Honey or levels from the GUI.
Supported GUI hit testing can use node bounds for card selection without moving purchase authority into presentation code.
Persistence retains platform/error/size constraints, so save v2 and v1-to-v2 migration continue through the existing protected storage abstraction rather than direct gameplay sys.save calls.

alternatives.reason: Matches D-007 exactly, keeps the progression surface to two evidence-backed tracks, exposes current/next/cost, preserves a meaningful first choice and makes the effect immediately measurable in production runtime.
A replacement for excluded Yield would exist only to fill a third card and would contradict the validated two-track decision.
Adds a second modal action to a low-frequency small purchase without evidence of destructive purchase errors or a comprehension problem requiring confirmation.
Removes the Flight-vs-Buzz choice and hides Honey spending, weakening the reward-to-choice loop.

findings: Blocking visual finding on the previous mechanically green runtime head: mobile Hive card copy was too small for the 844x390 target. The accepted head splits current->next/cost across rows and keeps both cards readable.

Blocking visual finding on the previous runtime head: the Lavender Buzz requirement was too close to the upper HUD. The accepted head renders explicit REQUIRES BUZZ 2 below the HUD and removes the gate when the capability is purchased.
No progression blocker remains: both first upgrades are affordable from 45 Honey, Flight changes real traversal, Buzz changes real work/gate capability, purchases are input-isolated and reload-safe.

Non-blocking scope limitation: P3 validates only the first Flight/Buzz level and uses repository-authored primitive development presentation; later effect curves and production art/audio remain later milestone work.

governance.trust_boundary_change: The P3 closeout updates gameplay/economy source-of-truth and evidence only; it does not change validator/workflow authority, branch rules, required checks or reviewer requirements.
governance.bypass_analysis: The PR changes economy/progression plus player-facing runtime/UI and high-risk Lua, so it remains classified economy and carries visual/evaluation evidence; it is not downgraded to process/trivial. The trusted validator continues to execute base/default-branch policy.
governance.rollback: Revert the P3 runtime/data/save-v2 changes together with P3 source-of-truth/evidence if later evidence invalidates the baseline. The migration is additive from P2 v1 and does not destructively rewrite campaign IDs/Honey.

known_limitations: Only Flight 1->2 and Buzz 1->2 are productionized in P3; later levels/effect curves remain tunable and require later pacing evidence.
30/35 Honey costs and 330 u/s / 1.35x effects are MEDIUM-strength runtime/simulation baselines, not final telemetry-locked balance.
Lavender is the first explicit Buzz gate; broader region gate cadence remains future content/pacing work.
P3 uses repository-authored primitive development UI/world presentation and the existing placeholder font; production illustration, animation, typography and audio polish remain later milestones.
Autonomous deterministic/browser evaluation is not a substitute for later external audience playtesting/telemetry.
